Plankton P/R rates, chamber comparison, and QC checks

Author

Jordan Vest

Published

September 18, 2026

Overview

This document summarizes respirometry runs measuring plankton production/respiration (P/R) rates from ambient coastal seawater samples at Kewalo. Samples were incubated in a temperature-regulated water bath (Inkbird controller) under alternating DARK and LIGHT conditions, with O2 and temperature logged continuously via PreSens optodes.

Starting with RUN3, we began testing chamber design as an additional variable — some samples were run in 350 mL BOD bottles, others in 500 mL mason jars, to check whether chamber geometry (bubble dynamics, surface area, etc.) meaningfully affects measured rates.

This report walks through: the rate-calculation pipeline, a chamber-type comparison, one sample exclusion and why, and a diagnostic check for whether LIGHT-period O2 increases reflect real photosynthesis or water-bath temperature drift.

Show code 
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(patchwork)

Data & Metadata

Sample metadata (incubation windows, site, chamber type/volume) lives in kewalo_respo_meta.csv and measurements_kewalo.csv. Every sample’s DARK/LIGHT time windows, chamber assignment, and any exclusions or truncations are tracked there — this report reads directly from those files rather than hardcoding anything, so it stays correct if the underlying data changes.

Show code 
RespoMeta <- read_csv(here("data","respirometry","kewalo","kewalo_respo_meta.csv"))
BioData   <- read_csv(here("data","respirometry","kewalo","measurements_kewalo.csv"))

RespoMeta %>%
  filter(run_block == "K_RUN4") %>%
  left_join(BioData, by = c("sample_ID","site_ID")) %>%
  select(sample_ID, site_ID, light_dark, start_time, stop_time, chamber_type, volume_mL, notes) %>%
  knitr::kable()

Rate Calculation Pipeline

Raw O2 traces (logged ~every 2 sec) are cut to each sample’s DARK/LIGHT window from the metadata, trimmed to drop the first 30 minutes (acclimation lag after each light transition), then thinned and fit with LoLinR::rankLocReg() — a bootstrapped method that finds the best local linear region of the trace rather than a single naive slope over the whole window, to avoid cherry-picking a fit by hand.

The code below is the actual for-loop from respo_seawater.R (shown, not executed here — a full run includes ~20+ bootstrapped regressions per sample and takes several minutes; see that script directly to re-run it against new raw data).

Show code 
for(i in 1:length(filenames_final)) {
  FRow <- as.numeric(which(Sample_Info$FileID_csv == filenames_final[i]))

  Respo.Data1 <- read_csv(skip = 1, file.path(path.p, file.names.full[i])) %>%
    dplyr::select(Date, Time, Value, Temp) %>%
    unite(Date, Time, col = "Time", remove = TRUE, sep = " ") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    mutate(Time = mdy_hms(Time))

  oxy_subsets <- Sample_Info[FRow,] %>%
    pmap(function(light_dark, start_time, stop_time, ...) {
      Respo.Data1 %>%
        filter(Time >= start_time & Time <= stop_time) %>%
        arrange(Time) %>%
        mutate(t_sec = as.numeric(difftime(Time, first(Time), units = "secs"))) %>%
        mutate(light_dark = light_dark) %>%
        filter(t_sec > 1800) %>%          # drop first 30 min (acclimation lag)
        filter(row_number() %% 10 == 0)   # thin to every ~20 sec
    })

  combined_oxy <- bind_rows(oxy_subsets)

  fit_reg <- function(data) {
    rankLocReg(xall = data$t_sec, yall = data$Value, alpha = 0.2, method = "pc", verbose = FALSE)
  }

  df <- combined_oxy %>%
    dplyr::select(t_sec, Value, Temp, light_dark) %>%
    nest_by(light_dark) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(regs = furrr::future_map(data, fit_reg),
           Temp.C = map_dbl(map(data, "Temp"), mean),
           RegStats = map(regs, function(x) x$allRegs %>% slice(1) %>%
                             dplyr::select(Intercept = b0, umol.L.sec = b1)))

  # ... intercept/slope extracted, joined to Sample_Info, written into RespoR
}

Rates are then converted to per-hour units using each sample’s actual chamber volume (volume_mL from measurements_kewalo.csv — 350 mL for BOD bottles, 500 mL for mason jars), and Respiration/NetPhoto/ GrossPhoto are derived per sample.

RespoR_PR %>%

  ggplot(aes(x = site_ID, y = Values, group = site_ID, color = site_ID, shape = run_block)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(run_block ~ PR, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Site", y = "µmol/hr") +

Sample Exclusion: S2.3_RUN4

During RUN4, S2.3’s probe came loose mid-run. The raw trace shows O2 sitting at a stable baseline (~360–380 µmol/L) for most of the LIGHT period, then spiking sharply to ~440 before crashing back to baseline — a signature inconsistent with a smooth biological trend, and consistent with a physical disturbance to the sensor.

Show code 
path_run4 <- here("data","respirometry","kewalo","rawo2","K_RUN4")

raw_s23 <- read_csv(skip = 1, file.path(path_run4, "S2.3_RUN4_O2.csv")) %>%
  dplyr::select(Date, Time, Value, Temp) %>%
  unite(Date, Time, col = "Time", sep = " ") %>%
  mutate(Time = mdy_hms(Time)) %>%
  drop_na()

ggplot(raw_s23, aes(x = Time, y = Value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.POSIXct("2026-09-01 13:45:00", tz = "UTC")),
             color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "S2.3_RUN4 — raw O2 trace", subtitle = "Dashed line: truncation point applied",
       y = expression(paste("O"[2], " (", mu, "mol/L)")))

Decision process:

  1. First attempt: truncate the LIGHT window’s stop_time to 13:45:00 (just before the spike begins), rather than discarding the whole sample — the goal was to keep whatever clean data remained.
  2. This left only ~15 minutes of usable data after the standard 30-minute acclimation cutoff — 9 data points after thinning, too few to trust a bootstrapped regression fit.
  3. Final decision: excluded S2.3_RUN4 entirely from the analysis (both DARK and LIGHT). The DARK-period data was clean, but with LIGHT unusable, NetPhoto/GrossPhoto couldn’t be calculated for this sample either way, and a Respiration-only data point without its paired photosynthesis measurement isn’t very useful for the P/R comparison.

This reasoning, along with the exact truncation timestamp and eventual exclusion, is recorded in the notes column of kewalo_respo_meta.csv for traceability — see that file directly for the row-level record.

Chamber Type Comparison

RUN3 and RUN4 include a mix of 350 mL BOD bottles and 500 mL mason jars, to check whether chamber design affects measured rates (e.g. via different bubble dynamics against the optode).

Show code 
RespoR_PR %>%
  filter(run_block %in% c("K_RUN3","K_RUN4")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = site_ID, y = Values, fill = chamber_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = chamber_type),
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(run_block ~ PR, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Site", y = "µmol/hr", fill = "Chamber Type", color = "Chamber Type") +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
Show code 
RespoR_PR %>%
  filter(run_block == "K_RUN4") %>%
  group_by(PR) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = tryCatch(t.test(Values ~ chamber_type)$p.value, error = function(e) NA)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
PR p_value
GrossPhoto 0.179
NetPhoto 0.456
Respiration 0.902

Note: sample sizes per chamber type are small (n = 4 per group in RUN4) — treat this as a preliminary check, not a definitive test. [Interpret result here once rendered.]

Temperature vs. O2 Diagnostic

Under LIGHT conditions, the water bath temperature shifts by about 1°C (vs. minimal drift in DARK) — partly driven by incubation light intensity, and partly by an ice pack added mid-run to counteract heating. This section checks whether LIGHT-period O2 increases reflect real productivity or are being driven by this temperature shift.

Show code 
acclim_sec <- 1800

RespoMeta_run4 <- RespoMeta %>%
  filter(run_block == "K_RUN4") %>%
  mutate(start_time = mdy_hms(paste(date, start_time)),
         stop_time  = mdy_hms(paste(date, stop_time)))

read_raw <- function(filename) {
  raw <- read_csv(skip = 1, file.path(path_run4, filename)) %>%
    dplyr::select(Date, Time, Value, Temp) %>%
    unite(Date, Time, col = "Time", sep = " ") %>%
    mutate(Time = mdy_hms(Time)) %>%
    drop_na(Time, Value, Temp) %>%
    arrange(Time)

  meta_rows <- RespoMeta_run4 %>% filter(FileID_csv == filename)

  meta_rows %>%
    pmap_dfr(function(light_dark, start_time, stop_time, ...) {
      raw %>%
        filter(Time >= start_time & Time <= stop_time) %>%
        mutate(t_sec = as.numeric(difftime(Time, first(Time), units = "secs"))) %>%
        filter(t_sec > acclim_sec) %>%
        mutate(light_dark = light_dark, sample_ID = sub("_O2.csv", "", filename))
    })
}

filenames_run4 <- list.files(path_run4, pattern = "csv$")
all_raw <- map_dfr(filenames_run4, read_raw)
light_only <- all_raw %>% filter(light_dark == "LIGHT")

Correlation summary (LIGHT period)

Show code 
light_only %>%
  group_by(sample_ID) %>%
  summarise(cor_temp_o2 = cor(Temp, Value, use = "complete.obs")) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(cor_temp_o2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
sample_ID cor_temp_o2
S2.2_RUN4 -0.87
S2.1_RUN4 -0.63
S1.2_RUN4 0.59
S2.4_RUN4 -0.52
S1.1_RUN4 -0.37
S1.4_RUN4 -0.35
S1.3_RUN4 0.25

Lag check (differenced, to control for shared trend)

Raw temp/O2 correlation and lag checks are inflated by the fact that both series are smoothly trending over the course of a LIGHT run — comparing consecutive changes instead of raw values removes this shared trend and isolates real moment-to-moment coupling.

Show code 
for (id in unique(light_only$sample_ID)) {
  sub <- light_only %>% filter(sample_ID == id)
  if (nrow(sub) > 5) {
    ccf(diff(sub$Temp), diff(sub$Value), main = paste(id, "- lag check (differenced)"))
  }
}

Interpretation: [Summarize once rendered — look for a single lag with a spike clearly above the significance band vs. scattered noise near zero across all lags. A flat/noisy pattern here, after differencing, supports that LIGHT-period O2 increases reflect real productivity rather than temperature drift. Any sample still showing a sharp spike at a consistent lag after differencing is worth flagging specifically.]

## Overview

This document summarizes respirometry runs measuring plankton production/respiration (P/R) rates from ambient
coastal seawater samples at Kewalo. Samples were incubated in a temperature-regulated water bath (Inkbird
controller) under alternating DARK and LIGHT conditions, with O2 and temperature logged continuously via
PreSens optodes.

Starting with RUN3, we began testing chamber design as an additional variable — some samples were run in
350 mL BOD bottles, others in 500 mL mason jars, to check whether chamber geometry (bubble dynamics, surface
area, etc.) meaningfully affects measured rates.

This report walks through: the rate-calculation pipeline, a chamber-type comparison, one sample exclusion
and why, and a diagnostic check for whether LIGHT-period O2 increases reflect real photosynthesis or
water-bath temperature drift.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(patchwork)
```

Sample metadata (incubation windows, site, chamber type/volume) lives in `kewalo_respo_meta.csv` and


## Rate Calculation Pipeline

Raw O2 traces (logged ~every 2 sec) are cut to each sample's DARK/LIGHT window from the metadata, trimmed to
drop the first 30 minutes (acclimation lag after each light transition), then thinned and fit with
`LoLinR::rankLocReg()` — a bootstrapped method that finds the best local linear region of the trace rather
than a single naive slope over the whole window, to avoid cherry-picking a fit by hand.

The code below is the actual for-loop from `respo_seawater.R` (shown, not executed here — a full run
includes ~20+ bootstrapped regressions per sample and takes several minutes; see that script directly to
re-run it against new raw data).

```{r}
#| label: for-loop-code
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: show

for(i in 1:length(filenames_final)) {
  FRow <- as.numeric(which(Sample_Info$FileID_csv == filenames_final[i]))

  Respo.Data1 <- read_csv(skip = 1, file.path(path.p, file.names.full[i])) %>%
    dplyr::select(Date, Time, Value, Temp) %>%
    unite(Date, Time, col = "Time", remove = TRUE, sep = " ") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    mutate(Time = mdy_hms(Time))

  oxy_subsets <- Sample_Info[FRow,] %>%
    pmap(function(light_dark, start_time, stop_time, ...) {
      Respo.Data1 %>%
        filter(Time >= start_time & Time <= stop_time) %>%
        arrange(Time) %>%
        mutate(t_sec = as.numeric(difftime(Time, first(Time), units = "secs"))) %>%
        mutate(light_dark = light_dark) %>%
        filter(t_sec > 1800) %>%          # drop first 30 min (acclimation lag)
        filter(row_number() %% 10 == 0)   # thin to every ~20 sec
    })

  combined_oxy <- bind_rows(oxy_subsets)

  fit_reg <- function(data) {
    rankLocReg(xall = data$t_sec, yall = data$Value, alpha = 0.2, method = "pc", verbose = FALSE)
  }

  df <- combined_oxy %>%
    dplyr::select(t_sec, Value, Temp, light_dark) %>%
    nest_by(light_dark) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(regs = furrr::future_map(data, fit_reg),
           Temp.C = map_dbl(map(data, "Temp"), mean),
           RegStats = map(regs, function(x) x$allRegs %>% slice(1) %>%
                             dplyr::select(Intercept = b0, umol.L.sec = b1)))

  # ... intercept/slope extracted, joined to Sample_Info, written into RespoR
}
```

Rates are then converted to per-hour units using each sample's actual chamber volume (`volume_mL` from
`measurements_kewalo.csv` — 350 mL for BOD bottles, 500 mL for mason jars), and Respiration/NetPhoto/
GrossPhoto are derived per sample.

## Sample Exclusion: S2.3_RUN4

During RUN4, S2.3's probe came loose mid-run. The raw trace shows O2 sitting at a stable baseline
(~360–380 µmol/L) for most of the LIGHT period, then spiking sharply to ~440 before crashing back to
baseline — a signature inconsistent with a smooth biological trend, and consistent with a physical
disturbance to the sensor.

```{r}
#| label: s23-raw-trace
path_run4 <- here("data","respirometry","kewalo","rawo2","K_RUN4")

raw_s23 <- read_csv(skip = 1, file.path(path_run4, "S2.3_RUN4_O2.csv")) %>%
  dplyr::select(Date, Time, Value, Temp) %>%
  unite(Date, Time, col = "Time", sep = " ") %>%
  mutate(Time = mdy_hms(Time)) %>%
  drop_na()

ggplot(raw_s23, aes(x = Time, y = Value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.POSIXct("2026-09-01 13:45:00", tz = "UTC")),
             color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "S2.3_RUN4 — raw O2 trace", subtitle = "Dashed line: truncation point applied",
       y = expression(paste("O"[2], " (", mu, "mol/L)")))
```

**Decision process:**

1. First attempt: truncate the LIGHT window's `stop_time` to 13:45:00 (just before the spike begins),
   rather than discarding the whole sample — the goal was to keep whatever clean data remained.
2. This left only ~15 minutes of usable data after the standard 30-minute acclimation cutoff — 9 data points
   after thinning, too few to trust a bootstrapped regression fit.
3. **Final decision: excluded S2.3_RUN4 entirely** from the analysis (both DARK and LIGHT). The DARK-period
   data was clean, but with LIGHT unusable, NetPhoto/GrossPhoto couldn't be calculated for this sample either
   way, and a Respiration-only data point without its paired photosynthesis measurement isn't very useful for
   the P/R comparison.

This reasoning, along with the exact truncation timestamp and eventual exclusion, is recorded in the
`notes` column of `kewalo_respo_meta.csv` for traceability — see that file directly for the row-level record.

## Chamber Type Comparison

RUN3 and RUN4 include a mix of 350 mL BOD bottles and 500 mL mason jars, to check whether chamber design
affects measured rates (e.g. via different bubble dynamics against the optode).

```{r}
#| label: chamber-plot
RespoR_PR %>%
  filter(run_block %in% c("K_RUN3","K_RUN4")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = site_ID, y = Values, fill = chamber_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = chamber_type),
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(run_block ~ PR, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Site", y = "µmol/hr", fill = "Chamber Type", color = "Chamber Type") +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r}
#| label: chamber-ttest
RespoR_PR %>%
  filter(run_block == "K_RUN4") %>%
  group_by(PR) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = tryCatch(t.test(Values ~ chamber_type)$p.value, error = function(e) NA)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

*Note: sample sizes per chamber type are small (n = 4 per group in RUN4) — treat this as a preliminary check,
not a definitive test. [Interpret result here once rendered.]*

## Temperature vs. O2 Diagnostic

Under LIGHT conditions, the water bath temperature shifts by about 1°C (vs. minimal drift in DARK) — partly
driven by incubation light intensity, and partly by an ice pack added mid-run to counteract heating. This
section checks whether LIGHT-period O2 increases reflect real productivity or are being driven by this
temperature shift.

```{r}
#| label: temp-o2-setup
acclim_sec <- 1800

RespoMeta_run4 <- RespoMeta %>%
  filter(run_block == "K_RUN4") %>%
  mutate(start_time = mdy_hms(paste(date, start_time)),
         stop_time  = mdy_hms(paste(date, stop_time)))

read_raw <- function(filename) {
  raw <- read_csv(skip = 1, file.path(path_run4, filename)) %>%
    dplyr::select(Date, Time, Value, Temp) %>%
    unite(Date, Time, col = "Time", sep = " ") %>%
    mutate(Time = mdy_hms(Time)) %>%
    drop_na(Time, Value, Temp) %>%
    arrange(Time)

  meta_rows <- RespoMeta_run4 %>% filter(FileID_csv == filename)

  meta_rows %>%
    pmap_dfr(function(light_dark, start_time, stop_time, ...) {
      raw %>%
        filter(Time >= start_time & Time <= stop_time) %>%
        mutate(t_sec = as.numeric(difftime(Time, first(Time), units = "secs"))) %>%
        filter(t_sec > acclim_sec) %>%
        mutate(light_dark = light_dark, sample_ID = sub("_O2.csv", "", filename))
    })
}

filenames_run4 <- list.files(path_run4, pattern = "csv$")
all_raw <- map_dfr(filenames_run4, read_raw)
light_only <- all_raw %>% filter(light_dark == "LIGHT")
```

### Correlation summary (LIGHT period)

```{r}
#| label: temp-o2-cor
light_only %>%
  group_by(sample_ID) %>%
  summarise(cor_temp_o2 = cor(Temp, Value, use = "complete.obs")) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(cor_temp_o2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

### Lag check (differenced, to control for shared trend)

Raw temp/O2 correlation and lag checks are inflated by the fact that both series are smoothly trending over
the course of a LIGHT run — comparing consecutive *changes* instead of raw values removes this shared trend
and isolates real moment-to-moment coupling.

```{r}
#| label: temp-o2-lag
#| fig-height: 4
for (id in unique(light_only$sample_ID)) {
  sub <- light_only %>% filter(sample_ID == id)
  if (nrow(sub) > 5) {
    ccf(diff(sub$Temp), diff(sub$Value), main = paste(id, "- lag check (differenced)"))
  }
}
```

**Interpretation:** [Summarize once rendered — look for a single lag with a spike clearly above the
significance band vs. scattered noise near zero across all lags. A flat/noisy pattern here, after
differencing, supports that LIGHT-period O2 increases reflect real productivity rather than temperature
drift. Any sample still showing a sharp spike at a consistent lag after differencing is worth flagging
specifically.]

## Summary for Discussion

- [ ] Chamber type effect: significant / not significant — see t-test above
- [ ] Temperature-driven artifact: present / not present — see differenced lag check above
- [x] S2.3_RUN4 excluded — probe disturbance, insufficient clean data post-truncation (see Sample Exclusion
      section)
- [ ] Open questions / next steps for follow-up
